title: What they say and what they intend
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Is what they say the same as what they want?
Jose said that a person may say yes, but their intention is not really to do it; their intention is something else that you do not know about.
He said that a truthful person might say: I have a lot of anxiety from this, this is terrible, in a plain way.
Jose said that people who are not lying in a business meeting are curious, enthusiastic, proactive and they follow up.
He said that with fraudulent people you see fleeting relationships. This is a general view of his, not a test, and is to be verified.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write a promise someone made you.
Write what else they might intend.
Write the question you would ask.
Write what you would need to see before you trust.

check.q: What did Jose say about a yes?
choices: The real intention may be different

check.q: What did he say honest people are?
choices: Curious, proactive and they follow up

check.q: What kind of view is this?

recap: Check intention against action. Treat these signs as clues, not proof.
